title: Homophones: words that sound the same
examples: When do I use there, their or they're?
Why is the k in knight silent?

explain.say: Say night, when the moon comes out. Now say knight, a soldier in armour. They sound exactly the same! Look at the board: in night, the letters i, g, h together make one long eye sound.

draw.text: Homophones: words that sound the same

explain.say: Now see the first box: kn. In knight, the k is silent. Words that sound the same but are spelled differently and mean different things are called homophones. Homo means same, phone means sound.
The most famous homophones are there, their and they're. Look at the first group: there is about a place, like over there. Here is a tip: the word here hides inside there, and both are places!
Now the middle group: their means it belongs to them, like their bags or their dog. Which word fits here? The children ate... their lunch, or there lunch?

Last group: they're is they are squashed together, and the apostrophe sits where the letter a was. Tip: if you can say they are, write they're. Well done! Challenge: fix this, Their going too the park.

faq.a: Homophones are words that sound the same but have different spellings and meanings, like night and knight, or sea and see.

faq.q: When do I use there, their or they're?
faq.a: Use there for a place, their when something belongs to them, and they're only when you could say they are.

faq.q: What is the difference between to, too and two?
faq.a: Two is the number 2. Too means also or very, like too hot. To shows direction or goes with a verb, like go to school or to eat.

faq.q: Why is the k in knight silent?
faq.a: About 1,000 years ago people did say the k in knight. Over time they stopped, but the spelling stayed the same.

faq.q: What is the difference between a homophone and a homonym?
faq.a: A homophone sounds the same but is spelled differently, like flour and flower. A homonym is spelled and said the same but means something different, like a bat that flies and a cricket bat.

facts: Homophone comes from Greek: homo means same and phone means sound.
In Old English the k in knight was pronounced.

quiz.say: The children forgot blank lunch boxes. Which word fits?
quiz.show: The children forgot ___ lunch boxes. Which word fits?
quiz.why: The lunch boxes belong to the children, so it is their.

wrong.0: there is for a place, not for belonging.
wrong.1: they're means they are, which does not fit.

quiz.why: Flour and flower sound the same but are spelled differently and mean different things.

wrong.1: These sound different; they are two forms of one verb.
wrong.2: These rhyme but start with different sounds.
